q: Rutherford's model states that an atom has a central nucleus and an electron or electrons revolve around it.
e: True. Rutherford's model states that an atom has a central nucleus and an electron or electrons revolve around it. Rutherford's scattering showed a tiny positive nucleus.

q: According to electromagnetic theory, orbiting electrons will emit radiation and finally they will collapse into the nucleus, which is a drawback of Rutherford's atomic model.
e: True. According to electromagnetic theory, orbiting electrons will emit radiation and finally they will collapse into the nucleus, which is a drawback of Rutherford's atomic model. Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium.

q: Bohr postulated that in an atom, an electron can move only in allowed circular orbits.
e: True. Bohr postulated that in an atom, an electron can move only in allowed circular orbits. Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum.

q: If an electron is moving in an allowed orbit, it absorbs and emits radiation continuously.
e: False. Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium.

q: An electron revolves around the nucleus in circular orbits with angular momentum $L$ which is an integral multiple of $h$, i.e., $L = nh$.
e: False. Angular momentum is L = Iω.

q: The postulate of angular momentum quantization states that $L = n \frac{h}{2\pi}$, where $n = 1, 2, 3, ...$ integer numbers.

Centripetal acceleration is v²/r toward the centre. It changes the direction of velocity, not the speed, when speed is constant.
